A deep sea port on the coast of Dubai, built in the late 1970s. It is the largest man-made harbour in the world and the busiest port in the Middle East.

Dubai's ruler Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum had it dug out of the desert shore south of the old town, at a time when many thought it far too big. He bet that Dubai, with little oil of its own, could live by trade and shipping, as it always had.

In 1985 a free zone opened beside the port. Foreign firms could own their companies outright, pay no tax and bring in workers, in a country where that was normally not allowed. Thousands of companies set up there, and the zone became a model copied across the Gulf and beyond.

Jebel Ali made Dubai the warehouse of the region, re-exporting goods to Iran, the rest of the Gulf, East Africa and South Asia. With Emirates airline and its airport, it turned the city into a world hub of the United Arab Emirates.
sum: A deep sea port on the coast of Dubai, built in the late 1970s. It is the largest man-made harbour in the world and the busiest port in the Middle East.
